references.text: Pharaoh's original command not to give the Israelites straw, yet still require the same amount of bricks, which led to the overseers' difficult situation.
The Israelite overseers were beaten because the people could not meet the daily quota of bricks.
The earlier description of the Israelites' forced labor and oppression in Egypt, which forms the background for the overseers' distress.
The overseers' complaint to Moses and Aaron as a result of the dire situation they found themselves in.
Israel's confession that the Egyptians treated them harshly and imposed hard labor on them, reflecting the experience of the overseers.
Both verses illustrate humanity's fundamental inability to bear the imposed demands (the workload in Exodus versus God's law in Hebrews).
